content_voiceover: This is the suggested treatment regimens table for first-line DLBCL therapy, and it's organized by clinical scenario rather than by stage alone. For stage one to two, excluding extensive mesenteric disease, the options are CHOP plus rituximab, or Pola-R-CHP, that's polatuzumab vedotin added to CHP plus rituximab, reserved for smIPI greater than one, both category one. For stage two with extensive mesenteric disease or stage three to four, CHOP plus rituximab and Pola-R-CHP for IPI two or higher remain preferred and category one, with dose-adjusted EPOCH plus rituximab as another recommended option. Two special populations get their own columns. Patients with poor left ventricular function need anthracycline-sparing or anthracycline-modified regimens, DA-EPOCH-R, CDOP which substitutes liposomal doxorubicin, CEOP which drops the anthracycline entirely, or GCVP with gemcitabine. Very frail patients and those over eighty with comorbidities get attenuated regimens, CDOP, mini-CHOP, or GCVP, all with rituximab. At the bottom, there's a dedicated box for concurrent CNS disease. Parenchymal CNS involvement is treated with systemic high-dose methotrexate at three grams per meter squared or higher, integrated into an anthracycline cycle, with the panel preferring day fifteen of a twenty-one day cycle. Leptomeningeal disease is treated with intrathecal cytarabine, methotrexate, and hydrocortisone, often through an Ommaya reservoir, plus systemic high-dose methotrexate, and consolidation with high-dose therapy and autologous stem cell rescue can be considered.
keypoints: Stage I-II: CHOP+R or Pola-R-CHP (smIPI >1), category 1
Stage II extensive mesenteric or III-IV: CHOP+R or Pola-R-CHP (IPI ≥2) preferred, category 1; DA-EPOCH+R also recommended
Poor LV function: anthracycline-sparing options, DA-EPOCH-R, CDOP, CEOP, GCVP + rituximab
Frail or age >80 with comorbidities: attenuated regimens, CDOP, mini-CHOP, GCVP + rituximab
CNS disease: high-dose methotrexate for parenchymal, IT triple therapy plus systemic methotrexate for leptomeningeal, consider HDT/ASCR consolidation
keypoint_voiceover: Match the regimen to the clinical scenario. Standard-risk stage one to two gets CHOP plus rituximab, or Pola-R-CHP if smIPI is greater than one. Higher-stage or bulky mesenteric disease gets the same backbone or dose-adjusted EPOCH. Poor cardiac function pushes you toward anthracycline-sparing regimens like CDOP or CEOP, while frailty or advanced age pushes you toward attenuated dosing like mini-CHOP. And for concurrent CNS disease, remember the two-tier approach, high-dose methotrexate integrated into chemotherapy for parenchymal disease, and intrathecal triple therapy plus systemic methotrexate for leptomeningeal disease.
